Where it began

Shakib Al Hasan was born on 24 March 1987 in Magura District, in the Khulna Division of Bangladesh. As a boy he was good enough to be paid to turn out for neighbouring villages, and he bowled fast in those days, with a tennis ball wrapped in tape. When Islampur picked him and handed him a real cricket ball for the first time, he took a wicket with his very first delivery.

He spent six months at the national sports institute, made his first-class debut for Khulna at 17, and in a youth tri-series final scored a hundred from 86 balls and took three wickets to win the trophy.

The player

He bowled slow left-arm spin and batted left-handed in the middle order, and he was good enough at both to be ranked the world's leading all-rounder in every format at one time or another. His one-day debut came in Zimbabwe in 2006 and his first Test in 2007, against India.

He played 71 Tests between 2007 and 2024, making 4,609 runs at 37.78, with five hundreds and a best of 217, and taking 246 wickets at 31.72, including 19 five-wicket hauls. His 7 for 36 against New Zealand at Chittagong in 2008 was, at the time, the finest return by any Bangladesh bowler. A year later, in the West Indies, he took over the captaincy at 22 when Mashrafe Mortaza was hurt, and led Bangladesh to their first series win abroad. In 2016 he captained them to their first Test victory over England.

What made him special

He did everything, and he kept doing it. In the 2019 World Cup he made 606 runs, more than anyone had ever scored in the group stage of the tournament, and in 2025 he became the first cricketer to reach 500 wickets and 7,000 runs in Twenty20 cricket.

He was a quick learner too. In his early Tests he was seen mainly as a batter, and his first wicket did not arrive until his fourth match. On a tour of South Africa he went through a whole day without one, took a coach's advice to toss the ball up, and claimed five the next day.

Away from the middle

He was the first Bangladeshi to play county cricket, for Worcestershire, and the first to appear in the Big Bash. Kolkata Knight Riders took two Indian Premier League titles with him in the side, in 2012 and 2014, and at home in the Bangladesh Premier League he was voted the best player of the season four times. In 2009 The Wisden Cricketer named him its Test Player of the Year, and Bangladesh honoured him with a National Sports Award.

And finally

Playing for Barbados Tridents in 2013, he bowled his four overs for six runs and took six wickets. Most bowlers would settle for that economy rate in a single over.
